questions.question:
다음 글을 읽고 순서로 알맞은 것은?

How smart are you with your money? These are the results of a survey of 250 students at Green Middle School. We first asked students "Are you smart with your money?"

(A) In short, our survey shows that the majority of students think they are not smart with their money. Managing money is not easy, and becoming a smart spender takes effort.

(B) 60% think they don't have enough allowance while 28% think they have difficulty saving money. Lastly, 12% said they spent money on things they didn't need.

(C) 70% answered "No" while 30% answered "Yes." We then asked the students who answered "No" what their biggest money worry is.
questions.explanation: 논리적 흐름을 보면: 먼저 설문 질문을 한 후 (C) 응답 결과를 제시하고, (B) 상세한 세부 결과를 보여준 다음, (A) 종합적인 결론을 제시하는 순서가 자연스럽다.

options: What was the first question of the survey?
How often do students get their allowance?
How many students participated in the survey?
How many students think they are smart with their money?
What percent of students think they don't have enough allowance?

How smart are you with your money? These are the results of a survey of 250 students at Green Middle School. We first asked students "Are you smart with your money?" 70% answered "No" while 30% answered "Yes." We then asked the students who answered "No" what their biggest money worry is. 60% think they don't have enough allowance while 28% think they have difficulty saving money. Q: Hello, Dr. Money. I'm Steve. I have difficulty ⓐsaved money. For example, I've been saving to go to my favorite singer's concert for the last two months. However, I still don't have enough money. I don't know ⓑwhat should do. A: Let's see. (A) In the last few weeks, you spent 80% of your allowance and only saved 20%. (B) I think you've been ⓒspent too much. (C) For example, you can follow the 50%-40%-10% rule. (D) Save 50%, spend 40%, and ⓓto donate the remaining 10% to charity. (E) By ⓔfollowing the rule, you can manage your money better.
questions.explanation: ⓐ saved→saving (have difficulty -ing), ⓑ what should do→what to do, ⓒ spent→spending (have been -ing), ⓓ to donate→donate (병렬구조). ⓔ following은 전치사 By 다음에 올바른 동명사 형태이다.

Q: Hello, Dr. Money. I'm Steve. I have difficulty saving money. For example, I've been saving to go to my favorite singer's concert for the last two months. However, I still don't have enough money. I don't know what to do. A: Let's see. (A) In the last few weeks, you spent 80% of your allowance and only saved 20%. (B) I think you've been spent too much.
